notes: First-generation migrants, i.e. born outside Australia. component_only: a post-hoc subgroup of one recruited cohort, split by country of birth. outcome_verbatim: The sample was divided into two groups based on job acquisition: those who obtained any kind of paid work, either formal or informal, for at least 30 days (EG), n=19, and those who did not (UG), n=26. | 'baseline clinical and neuropsychological data were compared between those who worked for at least 1 month during the 18-month follow up (employed group [EG]) and those who did not (unemployed group [UG]) ... In the present study, job acquisition was defined as 1 month of employment'
source_locator: Materials and methods, Statistical analysis, p. 37 (EG n=19, UG n=26); Materials and methods, Study design, p. 37 ('Of the 53 participants, 45 were followed up for 18 months'); Results, Sociodemographic data, p. 38 ('A total of 45 patients completed the study; of those, 19 (35.8%) acquired a job'); Discussion, p. 39 ('35.8% of all individuals gaining some work experience during the follow-up period')
conflict_note: THREE incompatible denominators for the same 19 people. (1) The Results sentence on p. 38 reads 'A total of 45 patients completed the study; of those, 19 (35.8%) acquired a job', but 19/45 = 42.2 per cent, not 35.8. (2) 19/53 = 35.85 per cent, and the Discussion on p. 39 describes the same figure as '35.8% of all individuals', which points at the enrolled sample of 53 rather than the 45 followed. (3) The job-duration breakdown on p. 38 gives 'Three individuals remained employed for less than 6 months (6.8%); six (13.6%) remained employed between 6 and 12 months and 10 (22.7%) for more than 12 months', and 3, 6 and 10 sum to the same 19 while 3/44, 6/44 and 10/44 give exactly 6.8, 13.6 and 22.7 per cent, implying a THIRD base of 44. CANDIDATE RESOLUTION, recorded but NOT applied: the analysed denominator is 45 (19 + 26, both printed as group sizes and both used as the bases of Tables 1 and 2), the 35.8 per cent was computed on the enrolled 53, and 44 is a further error. Under extraction_v3 rule 14 and D12.3d that reconstruction is not an authority, so the status stays unresolved pending an author reply.
notes: CONSTRUCT. Not paid_any, despite the phrase 'any kind of paid work'. The measure adds an explicit duration threshold, 'for at least 30 days' within the 18-month window, and everyone who worked for fewer than 30 days is counted as unemployed. Under D12.3a a threshold-defined result is precisely defined and is recorded as paid_intensity_threshold, never as paid_any and never as a substitute for it, because excluding everyone below the threshold changes the numerator while keeping a paid-employment label. The threshold is recorded in outcome_verbatim as required. ASCERTAINMENT. any_time_during_followup, not point prevalence: the numerator counts anyone who worked at any point during the 18 months, which is cumulative employment attainment and is synthesised separately under SAP 3.3. The paper's only point-prevalence figure is the 7 of 19 still working at the end of the study, recorded as a separate component_only row. MODERATORS. mean_age 34.23 is the mean of the ENROLLED 53, the only mean the paper prints; the 45 analysed have group means of 33.26 and 34.54 which the paper does not combine, and no weighted mean is typed here. n_female = 13 and n_post_secondary = 15 are sums of printed Table 1 cells on the 45 (female 5 + 8; higher education 7 + 8), which is why their denominator is 45 and not 53. perc_employed_baseline is left blank: the paper reports previous work experience but no baseline current-employment count.

outcome_verbatim: At the end of the study, only 7 EG participants (36.8%) were still working. [EG membership definition: 'those who obtained any kind of paid work, either formal or informal, for at least 30 days']
source_locator: Discussion, p. 39; group size from Materials and methods, Statistical analysis, p. 37
notes: JOB RETENTION, NOT A PREVALENCE. This is the only point-prevalence employment figure in the report, and it is recorded so that it is not lost, but it is component_only and enters no pool. Its denominator is the employed group, a subgroup defined BY the outcome: the 19 are exactly those who obtained paid work, so 7/19 is conditional on having worked and cannot estimate employment prevalence in the cohort. It is not extended to the full 45 either: the unemployed group is defined as not having worked for at least 30 days, which does not establish that none of them was working at month 18, so 7/45 would rest on an assumption the paper does not support and is NOT derived. 7/19 = 36.84 per cent, which matches the printed 36.8, so this row carries no conflict of its own, unlike the cohort row it sits inside.

source_locator: Table 3 'Employment outcomes for individuals in the Enhanced Vocational Rehabilitation (E-VR) or Thinking Skills for Work (TSW) programs over 3 years for the full study sample', p. 54; construct definitions 1.2.1 Work and school activity, p. 50; Results, p. 53
conflict_note: Table 3 (p. 54) prints the E-VR cell as '12/26' beside '48%'. 12/26 = 46.15 per cent, which does not round to 48; 12/25 = 48.00 per cent exactly. A denominator of 25 for E-VR is not arbitrary: Table 1 (p. 51) reports 'Any competitive work past 5 years' for E-VR as 23 yes and 2 no, which sums to 25 rather than 26. Both E-VR employment cells (any competitive work and any paid work) print 12 against 48 per cent, so the discrepancy is systematic within the arm rather than a single rounding slip; every TSW cell is internally consistent (16/28 = 57.1, 17/28 = 60.7, 21/28 = 75.0). The Discussion compounds it: 'vocational outcomes were relatively good, with 54% of total sample obtaining competitive work and 67% involved in some work related activity over the course of the study' (p. 55), whereas the table counts give 12 + 16 = 28 of 54 = 51.9 per cent competitive and 13 + 21 = 34 of 54 = 63.0 per cent any work activity. CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS, recorded but NOT applied: either the E-VR denominator is 25 and '/26' is the error, or the printed percentages are wrong and the counts stand. Choosing between them is a reconstruction, not an authority (extraction_v3 rule 14, D12.3d), so the status stays unresolved.
notes: Competitive work only. This is a paid-employment SUBTYPE and must not substitute for paid_any (SAP 3.1, extraction_v3 rule 5); the report gives a separate all-paid count, recorded as its own row. Ascertainment is cumulative over the whole three years, 'over the 3-year study', not status at 36 months, so it belongs to the cumulative-attainment synthesis and never to the point-prevalence pool. TRACKING COVERAGE. n_outcome_observed is set to the denominator Table 3 itself prints (12/26, 16/28 and so on), which is every randomised participant, but the paper also states 'Information on employment was available for all 54 participants (100%) during the 12 months of the study, for 52 (96%) participants in months 13-18, for 49 (88%) participants in months 19-24, for 46 (82%) participants in months 25-30, and for 42 (75%) participants in months 31-36' (1.2.1, p. 50). For a cumulative 'ever worked over three years' outcome, a quarter of the sample is therefore not observed for the final six months, which can only bias the numerator downwards. The paper states no handling method, so missing_data_method = not_stated and the issue is carried into the rob2_3_missing_outcome_data judgement rather than into a silent adjustment of the denominator.

source_locator: Results, p. 132 ('14 out of 29; 48%' and '6 out of 35'); measure definition 2.5.1.3 Supported employment, p. 131; analysis plan 2.6, p. 131; arm sizes Table 1, p. 132
notes: Arithmetic checks out: 14/29 = 48.3 per cent and 6/35 = 17.1 per cent, both matching the printed 48 and 17, and 29 + 35 = 64 randomised. No conflict on this result. CONSTRUCT IS `unclear`, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The report never establishes that the supported employment it counted is paid work. It gives no wage, no employer, no hours and no labour-market setting for the outcome, defines supported employment nowhere, and alternates between two different things: 'enrolled in supported employment' and 'supported employment enrollment status' describe entry to a SERVICE, while 'went on to secure supported employment' describes obtaining a JOB. SAP 3.1 excludes any activity for which remuneration or an employment relationship cannot be established, and the codebook is explicit that where a report does not establish the labour-market setting or the remuneration the value is `unclear` with the wording preserved. Coding it paid_competitive from the label alone would be the support-versus-setting error the vocabulary exists to stop, and coding it paid_any would put an unverified numerator into the primary construct. The one wage figure in the paper, 'Participants were paid $10 per hour worked', belongs to the four-month WORK THERAPY placement that BOTH arms received as a condition of entry, not to the supported-employment outcome, and that placement is itself described as 'not in conventionally competitive employment'. An author query is filed in unresolved_queries.md. ASCERTAINMENT is coded point_prevalence on the strength of the measures section, 'At follow-up, the number of participants in supported employment was tallied', and of the within-group McNemar tests, which compare enrolment status at two timepoints and therefore treat it as a status rather than as a cumulative event. The Results phrase 'by time of follow-up' points the other way and the ambiguity is recorded; it does not change eligibility, because the construct already blocks the row. MODERATORS: perc_female is typed from Table 1's printed 41 and 38 per cent because the source prints no female counts. perc_post_secondary is left blank: Table 1 gives mean YEARS of education (15.14 and 14.86), which is not a proportion with post-secondary education.

outcome_verbatim: Rate of employment, education and training [Table 2 row label]. Definition: 'employment status, categorised as being or not being in employment, education or training'
source_locator: Table 2 'Regression analysis of relationships between outcomes and occurrence of relapse', pp. 675-676; construct definition Method, p. 674; completion rates Results, p. 674; subgroup sizes Table 1, p. 675
conflict_note: The 190 participants with a 24-month employment, education and training status are split between the relapse groups in three mutually incompatible ways. (1) Table 2 (p. 676) prints 8/66 for those who relapsed and 30/124 for those who did not. (2) The Results text (p. 674) states 'Employment, education and training status was available for 70.7% of the participants who had relapsed and 77.2% of those who had not'; applied to the printed group sizes of 82 and 171 those give 58 and 132. (3) Table 4 (p. 676) reports employment-status change on 57 relapsers and 132 non-relapsers, total 189. The text percentages are not loose: the same sentence reproduces Table 2's MANSA denominators exactly (64.6 per cent of 82 = 53; 71.4 per cent of 171 = 122) and its PANSS denominators exactly (42.7 per cent of 82 = 35; 44.4 per cent of 171 = 76), so the method that generates 58 and 132 is demonstrably the method behind the other rows of the same table. Eight people are therefore attributed to the relapsed group in Table 2 that the text attributes to the non-relapsed group, which changes both printed rates (8/58 = 13.8 per cent rather than 12.1; 30/132 = 22.7 per cent rather than 24.2). CANDIDATE RESOLUTION, recorded but NOT applied: the group TOTAL is unaffected, because 66 + 124 = 58 + 132 = 190 and the numerators 8 + 30 = 38 either way, so the whole-cohort figure of 38/190 may well be correct even though the split is not. That is an inference about which of two printed splits is wrong and it is not an authority (extraction_v3 rule 14, D12.3d), and it does not establish that the numerators are correctly allocated either, so every row stays unresolved pending an author reply.
notes: Participants with at least one relapse of any severity during the trial. component_only: this is a POST-RANDOMISATION subgroup, defined by an event occurring after allocation, which SAP 2.1 explicitly bars from the prevalence estimand, and relapse is not randomised so it supports no randomised effect either. It exists here as a component of the whole-cohort total. n_outcome_observed is recorded as Table 2's printed 66 and NOT as the 58 implied by the Results text; the two are irreconcilable, which is why the row is blocked rather than adjusted.

MODERATORS: mean_age is left BLANK. The report prints no whole-cohort mean, only 44.25 in 82 relapsers and 47.30 in 171 non-relapsers; their sample-size-weighted mean is 46.3 years, which is recorded here in prose but not typed into the field, because it is this extractor's arithmetic rather than a printed value. perc_employed_baseline is also left BLANK on purpose: Table 1's baseline figure of 21/80 plus 53/171 in employment, education or training is an EET composite, not paid employment, and typing an EET proportion into a moderator named for baseline employment would overstate the baseline paid-work rate in every meta-regression that used it. Note also that Table 1 prints 21/80 as 25.3 per cent when 21/80 is 26.3 per cent.
